description: A comparator feeding a pulse counter: A minus B is weighed against a threshold, and each time that comparison goes high the count climbs one whole-tone step until it passes its limit

params.text: Sets the threshold the difference between the two signal inputs has to beat, -5V to +5V
Sets how far the count climbs before it drops back to zero, 1 to 31 steps
Scales the A input before B is subtracted from it, from silence to the whole signal
Scales the MAX CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the counter limit knob

inputs.text: One side of the comparison, scaled by its attenuator before B is taken away from it
Moves the counter limit, added to the limit knob through its attenuverter
The other side of the comparison, subtracted from the scaled A input

outputs.text: 5V while the scaled A input minus B is above the threshold, and 0V otherwise
5V at the moment the count drops back to zero while the comparator is high, and 0V otherwise
The count as a voltage, 0V to 5.17V in steps of 0.166V, which is a whole tone a step when it is patched as a pitch

notes: the counter limit knob starts fully down, where the count is cleared as soon as it moves, so VALUE stays at 0V and END repeats the comparator until the limit is turned up
the A attenuator also starts fully down, so a fresh module ignores whatever is patched into A
patching the A-B>T output back into B and setting the threshold negative makes the comparator flip every sample, which turns the module into an oscillator with the counter as its divider

inputs.1:
continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
